subject: Inflight priority lanes & SLA alignment for dedicated pool — Orion Biotech
messages:
From: Seth Palmer <seth.palmer@orionbiotech.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Torres <maya.torres@orionbiotech.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool SLAs — throughput & queue behavior

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking the time last week. We ran a short internal sanity run against the proof-of-concept and flagged two areas that matter for our production rollout:

- Sustained throughput guarantee (tokens/sec) for the reserved GPU nodes during peak windows
- Queueing behavior when the reserved pool is saturated — specifically whether we get deterministic prioritization for inflight requests or if requests are probabilistically evicted

We want to avoid user-facing tail latency spikes for our real-time annotator, so we need some clarity on:

1) How much headroom Redwood guarantees for burst windows before preemption or throttling kicks in;
2) What the remediation/credit model looks like if throughput drops below committed levels; and
3) If there is an option to designate a small percentage of the pool as "inflight-priority" (requests pinned to KV cache and not subject to batching evictions) — even if it's a paid carve‑out.

Could you send a short write-up or a proposed amendment to our commitment that spells this out? Also attaching the traces we collected during validation (small sample).

Appreciate it — Seth

--
Seth Palmer
Head of Platform Engineering
Orion Biotech
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Seth Palmer <seth.palmer@orionbiotech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool SLAs — throughput & queue behavior

Seth — thanks for the notes and the traces. Putting a short proposal below and attaching a draft amendment that formalizes the options. Quick summary up front:

- Reserved throughput: Redwood can commit to a sustained baseline (A) + burst headroom (B) during scheduled peak windows. Baseline is backed by reserved GPUs; burst headroom is best-effort but we can offer a contractual headroom guarantee up to X% for weekend or scheduled campaign windows.
- Inflight-priority carve-out: We can allocate a configurable percentage (we typically do 3–5%) of the pool as a priority lane. Requests in that lane get pinned KV cache and highest scheduling priority; they do incur a premium.
- Credits & remediation: If baseline throughput drops below committed level due to Redwood-side capacity issues, we provide pro-rated service credits. For tail-latency regressions we offer a tiered credit scale tied to the 99.9th percentile.

Specific asks for you: can you confirm target baseline tokens/sec for the baseline SLA, and how many simultaneous annotator sessions you expect during your peak 10-min window? That lets us size the carve-out.

Action items I've assigned to internal: Ben will size the priority-lane pricing, Laura will draft the formal SLA amendment and credit table. I attached a PDF draft for initial review.

Thanks — Ava

--
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Seth Palmer <seth.palmer@orionbiotech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool SLAs — throughput & queue behavior

Seth — quick technical clarity from our side on the priority lane and queueing model:

- Implementation: priority lane is implemented as a reserved scheduling class on the serving runtime. It pins a per-tenant KV cache allocation and bypasses the standard fair-share batch evictions for inflight tokens.
- Headroom: for a 5% priority carve-out on an N-GPU pool, practical headroom is baseline + ~40% for short bursts (<= 10 mins) because other pools still can offload work but cannot preempt the pinned requests.
- Preemption behavior: non-priority requests may be delayed or requeued; we do not force-kill in-progress priority requests unless there's a node-level failure.

Pricing note: the priority lane carries a 1.6x multiple on the reserved GPU unit price (covers pinned cache memory + scheduling overhead). I'll put a line item in the amendment.

Ben

From: Seth Palmer <seth.palmer@orionbiotech.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Maya Torres <maya.torres@orionbiotech.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 12:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool SLAs — throughput & queue behavior

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow ups from our infra team after reviewing your notes:

- Baseline target: 28k tokens/sec sustained across 8 reserved A100-class GPUs during our 10:00–11:00 daily campaign window. (This maps to ~140 concurrent annotator sessions under our config.)
- Carve-out ask: we want the priority-lane to cover at least 6 sessions (estimated ~2.4k tokens/sec) for critical interactive requests. Are you able to accommodate a smaller fixed number of pinned sessions rather than a percentage of the pool?
- Credits: we'd prefer a service credit approach that differentiates chronic under-provisioning (monthly misses) vs one-off incidents; can you propose thresholds for each?

Also, the draft amendment references a 99.9p tail; we need that to include an explicit measurement method (synthetic probe + customer-side telemetry agreement).

If you can share an updated amendment by tomorrow, we can start our procurement review and loop in legal.

Regards,
Seth
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Seth Palmer <seth.palmer@orionbiotech.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool SLAs — throughput & queue behavior

Seth — attaching an updated amendment (PDF link below) that folds in your numbers and a clearer credit model. Summary of changes:

- Baseline commitment: 28k tokens/sec across an 8-GPU reserved pool during 10:00–11:00 PT daily campaign window.
- Priority lane: option A — 6 pinned sessions (fixed allocation) priced at 1.9x per-session unit; option B — 4–6 dynamic pinned sessions (percentage fallback) priced at 1.6x. We included both to give procurement flexibility.
- Credit model:
  - Incident credit: if baseline drops >25% in a 10-minute window due to Redwood operational capacity, customer receives a 15% pro-rated credit for affected window.
  - Chronic credit: if monthly availability for committed baseline < 99.5%, customer receives a 50% pro-rated credit for the shortfall.
- Measurement: Redwood will publish 1-min synthetic probe results and accept customer-side telemetry as a secondary signal (screenshot + shared traces via Drive). Root cause analysis (RCA) timelines are 5 business days for operational incidents.

Next steps: if that aligns, we'll prepare a DocuSign amendment for signature and a short runbook (ops playbook) that details how we escalate and validate incidents. Link to amended PDF: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/redwood-sla-draft

Would you like us to include a 30-day canary with a reduced price for the first month? That can be used to tune the pinned session sizing.

Best,
Laura
